_what: THE ONE LIST of everything a client can do with Wingguy. Two things are generated from it by utils/wingguyCapabilities.js and there is no second copy of the words: the SHORT answer to "what can I do with Wingguy?" (wingguy_vision in services/wingguyGetStartedMcp.js) and the FULL page at knowaguy.com.au/what-wingguy-can-do (routes/marketingRoutes.js). Checked by tests/wingguy-capabilities.test.js.
_why: 9 Nov 2026: the answer a brand-new client got on onboarding day never mentioned their Linked Helper machine, still said leads arrive by copy and paste, and was missing half of what had been built since July. It was hand-written prose, so nothing made it keep up. Now a new tool cannot ship without a line here - the test fails until it has one.
_rules: Built a new tool? Add it to an item's tools here (or a new item), or to not_shown with the reason. Then run: node tests/wingguy-capabilities.test.js

say: the sentence the client types. It must already be in content/client-phrases.json when the item has tools - that is the house rule for any sentence a client is told to type, and the test enforces it.
does: what it DOES, in Guy's plain English, before what it is called. Short dash ' - ', never an em dash. Say 'instructions', never 'rules'. No praise of Wingguy's own drafting.
tools: every MCP tool that sits behind this line. The first one is the tool the say-sentence must be registered against.
needs: machine | mailbox | calendar | notes - when the client has not connected that yet, the line is still shown, marked as opening up once they do.
added: YYYY-MM-DD for a new feature. The line carries a 'New' flag for 30 days from that date, then drops it by itself.
not_shown: tools deliberately left out of the client answer (Guy-only, or the answer itself), each with the reason.
short (per section): one plain line saying what that part does for them - it is the summary in the chat answer and on the closed card of the page.
start: true on the handful of lines a brand-new client should try first - they make the 'Start with these' strip at the top of the page.

sections.title: Your machine - it finds the people
sections.short: Finds the right people on LinkedIn and invites them, every week, by itself.
sections.lead: It runs **Linked Helper**, software that works LinkedIn for you like a careful assistant. It sends connection requests to exactly the people you've picked, up to 100 a week, spread over sensible hours so it looks like a real person at work. It lives on your own computer in the cloud, so it's always on and there's no laptop to leave running. Guy built it, it gets checked every day and backed up every night, and if LinkedIn ever signs you out you get an email. You run it from right here:

items.does: your own link, straight in from any browser.
invitations sent, how many said yes, and how many people are still waiting. The same numbers land in your inbox every Monday.
see the message it sends, the days and times it runs and how many go out a week - then change any of it in plain English. I show you the change before I make it.

items.say: top up my campaign with this search
items.does: paste a LinkedIn search link and I add those people, so it never runs dry.
every campaign your leads are coming from, and how many each has brought in.

items.say: put this file on my machine
items.does: get a file or a line of text from your computer onto the machine without any fiddling.

sections.title: Every yes lands with me, already sorted
sections.short: Everyone who says yes arrives read and scored, best first.
sections.lead: When someone accepts, they show up in your leads by themselves - profile read, and scored against who you're really after, so the best people come first.

items.does: change what a good lead looks like for you, test it on real people before anything is saved, and undo it if you don't like it.

items.say: who is Sarah and what's her email?
items.does: one lookup across your leads and everyone you've written to.
someone you met another way, or a person you've just been introduced to, goes in properly. Fix a city, email or phone the same way, or tag people into a list.
the website where you work your leads.

sections.title: Then I look after every conversation
sections.short: Nobody you owe a reply slips through.
sections.lead: Nobody falls through the cracks. The list is worked out overnight, so it's ready when you sit down.

items.does: everyone you owe something, best first, with the drafts already written. Park someone until a date, or drop them for good.
rebuild the list right now if a lot has changed.
your whole history with anyone in one go - calls, emails, LinkedIn, what you agreed last time.
off their real profile and what they post, on your instructions, never a template.
the people who went quiet months ago, sorted into worth reopening and let go, with the reopening notes written.
the people you already know on LinkedIn are worth the most. I find the old conversations worth picking up and bring you a few each day.

sections.title: Your email, without living in it
sections.short: Drafts in your own mailbox. You press send.
sections.lead: Everything is written into your own mailbox as a draft. I never send. That is always you.

items.does: a real draft in your Drafts folder, links intact, on the right thread.

items.say: what did she say in her last email?
items.does: I read it to you, or show the whole back-and-forth with one person and what you've already sent them.
sorted into what needs you, what's just for your info and what can go. Clearing them out works on Gmail today, and nothing goes without your yes.

sections.title: Your diary and your bookings
sections.short: Real free times, offered and booked.
sections.lead: Real free times, with your hours, buffers and time zones already applied.

items.does: today's diary plus everything I know about who you're meeting. Guy starts every morning this way.
three real slots that suit you both - and if they sent a booking link, I read it and find where you overlap.
the invite, your meeting link and the reminders, all sent. Move or cancel it later just by saying so.

sections.title: Your calls, remembered
sections.short: Every recorded call kept against the right person.
sections.lead: Every recorded call is kept against the right person, so the follow-up writes itself.

items.say: draft the follow-up from my last call
items.does: I read the transcript and write the email from what was actually said.

items.say: here's the transcript from a call you missed
items.does: paste it in and I file it against the right person.
see every call I keep, stop one before it's stored, or delete any of it for good. It's your data.

sections.title: It gets more like you every week
sections.short: Everything is written on your own instructions.
sections.lead: Everything I write runs on your own instructions, and you change them in plain English.

items.does: a guided chat that turns the starter kit into your voice - your angle, who you're after, how you handle a no.
tell me what to do differently. I show you the change before I make it, it sticks for good, and you can always go back.

items.does: your banned words, gone from every draft.

items.say: add this article to my library

sections.lead: I don't only do the work - I teach you Guy's whole method as you go, in his words, not generic advice off the internet. And it grows: what Guy learns with every client lands in your Wingguy automatically.
